property_summary: Only the current owner can change `owner`: for any caller and any new owner, a `transferOwnership` call by a non-owner reverts (or by the owner sets owner to the new owner) so `c.owner()` always equals the last owner-set value; the mutant lets any caller change `owner`, so a non-owner call succeeds and `owner` differs.

Only the current owner (initially address(0)) may transfer ownership, so transferOwnership must revert and leave owner unchanged for any non-owner caller; the inverted modifier lets any non-owner succeed and change owner, which the test detects.

For any non-owner caller, transferOwnership must revert (or leave owner unchanged); the buggy version lets any caller set owner to any value, so after the call c.owner() equals the fuzzed new owner in M but stays address(0) in P.

After the current owner calls transferOwnership(newOwner), the contract's owner must equal exactly newOwner for every input; the mutant sets owner to msg.sender instead, so for any newOwner != msg.sender the rule is violated.
For every caller that is not the current owner, owned() must revert; the buggy modifier inverts the check, so any non-owner call succeeds, violating the rule.
Any non-owner (owner is address(0) initially, so every non-zero caller) must have calls to owned() revert; the mutant drops the check so such calls succeed, violating the rule.
m_diagnostic: testFuzz_property(address): non-owner must not be able to call owned()

property_summary: For any caller that is the current owner and any new owner address, calling transferOwnership(newOwner) must make owner() equal exactly newOwner; the mutant instead sets owner to the zero address, so for any non-zero newOwner the invariant owner() == newOwner fails.

For any fuzzed newOwner (nonzero), calling transferOwnership(newOwner) as the current owner must set the public owner variable to exactly newOwner; the mutant never updates owner, so the getter returns the old owner and breaks this for some input.
For any caller that is not the current owner, transferOwnership must leave owner unchanged; the mutant lets any caller set owner, so it violates this for some non-owner caller.

For any caller, invoking owned() either reverts (non-owner) or leaves the owner state unchanged: owned() must never mutate c.owner(). The reference satisfies this for every input; the mutant breaks it because owned() writes owner = msg.sender, which diverges from the pre-call owner for a caller that is not the owner at call time.

For any fuzzed caller, a call to owned() must either revert (caller is not the owner) or leave the owner unchanged — owned() is a state no-op; the mutant writes owner = msg.sender inside owned(), so a successful owned() call diverges from the owner value established solely by transferOwnership.

For any fuzzed caller, a call to owned() is either rejected by onlyOwner or is a state no-op, so after owned() plus a subsequent transferOwnership(fuzzed newOwner) the owner getter must equal exactly the value passed to transferOwnership — the mutant instead overwrites owner with msg.sender inside owned(), breaking this equality whenever the second caller differs from the last transferred owner.

After transferOwnership(newOwner), a subsequent call to owned() by any fuzzed caller must either revert or leave the owner exactly equal to newOwner — owned() must never change ownership — which the mutant breaks because owned() writes owner = msg.sender, diverging whenever the caller differs from the transferred owner at the moment the write lands.
